## PSet 1: The Price of Housing

## My work

### Understanding the data

- Variables:

  - **fips** (code describing state, county, and county subdivision), **stups** (state postal code)

  - **state** (2 digit state code), **countyname** (county name), **county_town_name** (Town Name for areas in New England)

  - **hud_area_code** (HUD-assigned identification number for FMR areas), hud_area_name (name of area)

  - **metro** (1= metropolitan statistical area area, 0 = not),

  - **pop2024** (population in 2024)

  - **bedrooms** (# of bedrooms)

  - **fmr** (fair market rent)

  - Further description

    - Fair Market Rents

      - Cost of shelter (rental payment agreed to in lease) + utilities (regardless of who pays)

      - Used to determine

        - payment standard amounts for Section 8 housing choice voucher program

        - public housing flat rents

        - renewal funding inflation factor calculations

        - rent ceilings (for HOME rental assistance program, Emergency Solutions Grants program)

        - input for other formulas (e.g. HUD's calculation of very-low income limits)

    - Metropolitan

      - Based on core-based statistical areas

      - Before 2000, metro areas based on towns - this distinction has remained for town-based metro area definitions in New England

- Data collection

  - Collected by HUD (department of Housing and Urban Development)

  - FMRs used within variety of housing assistance programs, representing HUD's best estimate of the 40th percentile of rents paid by recent movers with various housing markets

  - Process

    - Uses data from the U.S. Census Bureau’s American Community Survey (ACS)

    - Area Rent surveys

      - Sample of telephone numbers / addresses surveyed

      - Mail surveys

    - Focus on recent movers (to reflect current pricing)

    - Adjust figures for inflation

- Each row gives Fair Market Rent (for fiscal year 2027) for a particular county/county equivalent/New England town, by number of bedrooms.

  - HUD estimates FMR for whole hud area, not for counties within area

- Observations from code

### Code

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# read in data
df <- read.csv("data/fmr2027.csv")

# data clean up
df <- rename(df, stusps = state, state = stusps)

df$metro <- factor(df$metro, 
              levels = c(0, 1), 
              labels = c("non-metro", "metro"))

# view data
head(df)

# 2 bedrooms as a "standard" rental size
two_bedrooms <- filter(df, bedrooms == 2)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(distinct(df, fips, pop2024), mapping = aes(x = pop2024)) + 
  geom_histogram(bins = 40) + 
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) + 
  labs(caption = "Figure 1")
# DISTRIBUTION COUNTY POPULATION SIZES
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(data = two_bedrooms, mapping = aes(fmr)) + 
  geom_histogram()  + 
  labs(caption = "Figure 2")
# DISTRIBUTION 2 BEDROOM RENTS
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(data = df, aes(x = factor(bedrooms), y = fmr, fill = metro)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(caption = "Figure 3")
#DISTRIBUTION FMR PER BEDROOM, METRO VS. NON-METRO
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(data = df, mapping = aes(x = pop2024, y = fmr, color = metro)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar)  +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
    labs(caption = "Figure 4")
# POPULATION VS. FMR, METRO VS. NON-METRO
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| fig-height: 9
ggplot(two_bedrooms, 
       aes(x = fmr, y = reorder(state, fmr, FUN = median))) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(caption = "Figure 5")
# BOXPLOT 2BR FMR BY STATE
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| fig-height: 9
two_bedrooms <- filter(df, bedrooms == 2)
by_state <- group_by(two_bedrooms, state, metro)
state_medians <- summarize(by_state, twoBR_median_fmr = median(fmr, na.rm = TRUE))

ggplot(state_medians, 
       aes(x = twoBR_median_fmr, 
           y = reorder(state, twoBR_median_fmr), 
          color = metro)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(caption = "Figure 6")

# MEDIAN 2BR FMR BY STATE, METRO VS. NONMETRO
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| fig-height: 9
state_counts <- count(two_bedrooms, state)
ggplot(state_counts, aes(x = n, y = reorder(state, n))) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(caption = "Figure 7")
# COUNTIES PER STATE
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
hud_area_counts <- count(two_bedrooms, hud_area_code)

ggplot(hud_area_counts, aes(x = n)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(caption = "Figure 8")
# COUNTIES PER HUD AREA
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
four_bedrooms <- filter(df, bedrooms == 4)
four_only <-  dplyr::select(four_bedrooms, fips, fmr_4 = fmr)
both <- inner_join(two_bedrooms, four_only, by = "fips")

ggplot(data = both, aes(x=fmr, y=fmr_4, color = metro)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .3) +
  labs(caption = "Figure 9")
# FMR 2 BEDROOM VS 4 BEDROOM
```
